title: Be a Mirror
coreMove: Echo the loaded few words and hold the silence so the other person expands the truth on their own.
sourcePressure: The source defines mirroring as repeating the last or critical one to three words, using a calm late night FM DJ voice, slowing the conversation, allowing silence, and testing how solid the other side's position is.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer must not portray mirroring as parroting whole sentences, agreeing, or using a fake listening trick.

hook: Someone repeats the last word and magically wins
A customer-service script with polite echoing
tryThisNow: Repeat the last three words today

exampleSpecs.domain: airport gate rebooking after a mechanical delay
exampleSpecs.audience: a gate supervisor facing a passenger who says the airline ruined a custody handoff
exampleSpecs.stakes: the passenger may miss the legally scheduled exchange unless the real constraint surfaces
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the supervisor mirrors 'custody handoff' in a low voice and stays quiet until the passenger explains the court-ordered time window
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a boarding scanner blinking red beside a stack of delayed-flight meal vouchers

exampleSpecs.audience: a procurement lead trying to learn whether a supplier's impossible delivery claim is firm
exampleSpecs.stakes: a regional bread run may be canceled if the flour blend is truly unavailable
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the lead mirrors 'absolutely no pallets' and lets the silence run until the supplier admits two partial pallets are held for another buyer
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a flour-dusted purchase order beside a scale ticket from the loading dock

exampleSpecs.audience: a shelter coordinator speaking with a resident refusing to register
exampleSpecs.stakes: the family may leave without medication access because the privacy fear remains unnamed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coordinator mirrors 'government list' and waits until the resident explains an immigration concern that changes the intake path
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a folding cot tag clipped to a clipboard under fluorescent gym lights

exampleSpecs.audience: a registrar trying to understand why a partner museum says the loan is impossible
exampleSpecs.stakes: a centerpiece exhibit may open with an empty case if the true condition is not discovered
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the registrar mirrors 'not stable enough' and says nothing until the counterpart explains the vibration limit in the freight contract
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a foam-lined crate diagram spread under a conservation lamp

exampleSpecs.domain: regional rail maintenance dispatch during signal failure
exampleSpecs.audience: a dispatcher trying to locate the real cause of a crew's refusal to clear a track
exampleSpecs.stakes: commuter service will cascade into cancellations if the hidden safety concern stays vague
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the dispatcher mirrors 'not putting anyone on that section' and waits through the radio hiss until the crew names the wet junction box
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a green track diagram frozen on a dispatch wall at 5:18 p.m.

exampleSpecs.domain: special-events permit review for a street festival
exampleSpecs.audience: a nonprofit organizer hearing that the permit is not acceptable
exampleSpecs.stakes: the festival loses its food vendors unless the city reviewer reveals the exact blockage
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after a failed defense of the application, the organizer mirrors 'not acceptable as submitted' and the reviewer finally points to the fire-lane diagram
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a rolled street-closure map held flat by two permit stamps

skillTargets: select the phrase worth mirroring from a tense statement
distinguish mirroring from agreement or paraphrase
analyze how silence after a mirror changes information flow
evaluate when a mirror would be too mechanical or unsafe

tryThisNowSpec: When someone gives you a loaded reason, pick the one to three words with the most heat, repeat only those words in a calm voice, and let the next silence finish before you speak again.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm — a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
